chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Witr prayer: is it separate or connected? He said, 'Separate.'
ai.seo_question: Is the Witr prayer considered separate or connected in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the jurisprudential status of Witr by ruling it as 'fasl' (separate), distinguishing it from the continuous flow of the preceding night prayer. This ruling underscores the Shia preference for treating Witr as an independent act of worship rather than a concluding segment of Tarawih or Tahajjud, a view supported by the majority of Shia jurists to preserve its distinct legal identity.
